[title] Survey Results Summary statistics Quantiles and boxplots Python/Colab Outlook Using boxplots
[body] A boxplot1 displays the distribution of data
[body] • Useful for identifying outliers • Efficient for comparing multiple datasets • The lines indicating the “maximum/minimum” points (excluding outliers) are called whiskers
[body] 1Figure source: https://towardsdatascience.com/understanding-boxplots-5e2df7bcbd51
[body] Prof. Oke (UMass Amherst) CEE 260/MIE 273 M1b: Summarizing Data September 10, 2026 13 / 16

FIGURE: [description of the image, not printed words] A horizontal numerical axis runs from −4 to 4. A pink rectangular box spans approximately −0.7 to 0.65, with a yellow vertical line at 0 and black vertical edges at Q1 and Q3. A thin blue horizontal line extends to black vertical marks near −2.7 and 2.7. Two green circular points lie near −3.0 and −2.8; two lie near 2.8 and 3.0. Labels include “Outliers,” “Interquartile Range (IQR),” “Minimum” (Q1 − 1.5*IQR), “Maximum” (Q3 + 1.5*IQR), Q1 (25th Percentile), Median, and Q3 (75th Percentile).

novice.takeaway: A boxplot summarizes a data distribution using quartiles and the median, while whiskers show the non-outlier minimum and maximum and separate outliers can be spotted.
questions: How is the interquartile range calculated?
novice.inferred_claim: Use boxplots to compare datasets and identify outliers.

peer.takeaway: A boxplot summarizes a distribution with quartiles, median, whiskers, and separately marked outliers, making outlier detection and dataset comparison easier.

expert.takeaway: A boxplot summarizes a distribution with quartiles, median, IQR, whiskers extending to the non-outlier extremes, and separately plotted outliers.
